blocks.explanation:
Same idea as Question 13, with whole angles.
From \(\alpha + \beta = 180^{\circ} - \gamma\) take the cotangent of both sides.
Plan: allied angle on the right, cot-sum formula on the left, cross-multiply, collect.
steps:
Take cot of both sides
\[\alpha + \beta = 180^{\circ} - \gamma\]
\[\cot(\alpha + \beta) = \cot(180^{\circ} - \gamma) = -\cot\gamma\]
Why: \(180^{\circ} - \gamma\) is in quadrant II where cot is negative; \(180^{\circ}\) is an even multiple of \(90^{\circ}\), so cot stays cot.

Expand the left side
\[\dfrac{\cot\alpha\cot\beta - 1}{\cot\alpha + \cot\beta} = -\cot\gamma\]
Why: Cot-sum formula (Question 6(i)).

Cross-multiply
\[\cot\alpha\cot\beta - 1 = -\cot\gamma\cot\alpha - \cot\gamma\cot\beta\]
Why: Multiply both sides by \(\cot\alpha + \cot\beta\) and open the bracket.

Collect the products
\[\cot\alpha\cot\beta + \cot\beta\cot\gamma + \cot\gamma\cot\alpha = 1\]
Why: Move the two products to the left and the 1 to the right.

Check with \(60^{\circ}\) each
\[3\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 = 3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{3} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(\cot 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\); the sum of the three products is 1.
